series.name: Data centers: community growth and jobs
series.question: Agreement that AI data centers would substantially improve local economic growth and employment.
series.population: US adults age 18+, including Alaska and Hawaii

point_details.population: US adults age 18+, including Alaska and Hawaii
point_details.question_paraphrase: Agreement that AI data centers would substantially improve local economic growth and employment.
point_details.methodology: English online nonprobability survey of 1,078 adults age 18+ in the continental US, Alaska and Hawaii. Recruitment used Ipsos and partner panels plus river sampling, without a traditional population sampling frame. Raking used March 2025 CPS targets for gender, age, race/ethnicity, region and education. Ipsos reports a 3.6-point credibility interval and a design-effect-adjusted interval of 5.1 points (DEFF 1.5); this is not a conventional sampling margin of error.
point_details.uncertainty_type: Ipsos credibility interval for nonprobability survey

series.note: One verified wave. These are separate agree/disagree statements, not mutually exclusive response options. Use reported net percentages, which can differ from sums of rounded components. Do not connect to Reuters/Ipsos local opposition. Ipsos reports a 3.6-point credibility interval, or 5.1 points after design-effect adjustment. This is an online nonprobability sample.

series.name: Data centers: concern that ai raises electricity costs
series.question: The electricity required to use AI could make electricity more expensive

point_details.question: The electricity required to use AI could make electricity more expensive
point_details.methodology: English probability-based Ipsos KnowledgePanel survey of 4,531 US adults age 18+. Weights adjust gender by age, race/ethnicity, region, metropolitan status, education, income, 2024 vote and party identification. Full-sample margin of sampling error is +/-1.5 percentage points at 95% confidence, including design effect 1.05.
point_details.publication_note: The June poll landing page is dated June 8; the dedicated data-center analysis is dated June 12. The currently linked PDF is hosted in a 2026-08 directory; this directory is not the fieldwork or original release date.

series.note: One verified wave. Respondents assessed concern about a possible future cost; this is not evidence that AI actually increased electricity bills. The reported net is 77%; summing rounded components (48 and 28) would incorrectly give 76%.

series.name: Data centers: support local data centers
series.question: Overall, would you (oppose) or (support) the construction of new data centers in your area?

point_details.question: Overall, would you (oppose) or (support) the construction of new data centers in your area?
point_details.methodology: Annenberg Public Policy Center probability panel operated by SSRS, primarily online with a small telephone component, targeting noninstitutionalized US citizens age 18+. Weighted to national benchmarks. The published topline reports both waves under the same AI7 question; unknown/refused responses remain in the denominator. Summer retained 1,241 spring respondents (93% retention), so this is a panel comparison.
point_details.publication_note: Spring values are reproduced in the August topline; the linked spring article was published May 14. This is the August report vintage, not an assertion that the spring observation first became public in August.
